data.title: Alligator Bioscience provides an update on the company's financial position
data.description:
Lund, Sweden, 27 November 2026 – Alligator Bioscience (Nasdaq Stockholm: ATORX) provides an update on the company's financial position following the completed rights issue and the sale of mitazalimab to Biossil

On 22 September 2026, Alligator announced the final outcome of the rights issue of units. Alligator initially received approximately SEK 58.8 million before issue costs and repayment of bridge loans of SEK 19 million.

In October 2026, Alligator sold all rights to mitazalimab, including its derivatives, to Biossil, Inc. Alligator received an upfront payment of USD 0.75 million and is eligible for milestone payments of up to USD 108 million, as well as mid-single-digit royalties on future sales. From closing, Biossil is responsible for all further development, manufacturing, and patent costs, which means that Alligator do not carry any future costs associated to mitazalimab. With the divestment of mitazalimab, milestones and royalties from HLX22 and mitazalimab represent the majority of Alligator's future value stream.

Following these transactions, Alligator assesses that its existing cash is sufficient to fund operations through 31 December 2027. The assessment does not take into account repayment of the loan from Fenja Capital (approximately SEK 7 million, due in June 2027) or any proceeds from exercise of the TO 15 warrants in January 2027.

Topline data from Henlius' Phase 3 study of HLX22 in first-line HER2-positive gastric cancer is expected in the second half of 2027.

The TO 15 warrants can be exercised for subscription of new shares from 8 to 22 January 2027.

Alligator will update the market when there is new material information. Alligator only comments on the HLX22 programme when updates are shared through official channels, such as by Henlius or in publicly registered clinical trial information. The same policy applies to any new material information relating to mitazalimab.

For further information, please contact:

Søren Bregenholt, CEO

E-mail: soren.bregenholt@alligatorbioscience.com

Phone: +46 (0) 46 540 82 00

Johan Giléus, CFO

E-mail: johan.gileus@alligatorbioscience.com

Phone: +46 (0) 46 540 82 00

The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact person set out above, at 4:00 p.m. CET on 27 November 2026.

About Alligator Bioscience

Alligator is a biotechnology company with financial interests, through milestone payments and royalties on future sales, in two programmes: HLX22, an anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody being developed by Shanghai Henlius Biotech Inc., and mitazalimab, an anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody, including its derivatives, being developed by Biossil, Inc. Alligator also holds an interest in the antibody ALG.APV-527, co-developed with Aptevo Therapeutics Inc., as well as in the bispecific antibody format RUBY™.

Alligator is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ATORX) and headquartered in Lund, Sweden.

data.title: Altria’s Potential Acquisition Of Imperial Brands Is ‘No Doubt Accretive,’ Says Stifel
data.description:
Key points:
  • Altria said any potential offer for Imperial Brands would likely be entirely in cash.
  • Stifel maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on Altria with an $82 price target.
  • Jefferies said Altria could consider selling its stake in AB InBev to fund Imperial’s acquisition

Wall Street sees strategic and financial benefits from Altria Group’s (MO) potential acquisition of British tobacco giant Imperial Brands (IMBBY), with Stifel stating Altria’s balance sheet and its equity stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev “provide ample capacity” for the deal.

MO shares were down 2.5% at the time of writing.

Altria Confirms Media Report, Says It Is Considering Acquisition

On Thursday, Altria said that it was considering a possible all-cash offer for Imperial Brands. The company also said that it was in discussions with a third party over the potential acquisition of part of Imperial’s business.

However, Imperial Brands denied having held discussions with or received a proposal from Altria or any third party.

The statements came after Bloomberg reported Thursday that Altria Group and Japan Tobacco were exploring a potential takeover of the British cigarette maker.

Altria sells Marlboro cigarettes in the U.S. and owns the nicotine pouch brand on!. Imperial Brands’ portfolio includes Davidoff and Gauloises cigarettes, Golden Virginia rolling tobacco and blu vaping products. Under takeover rules in the U.K., Altria has until December 24 to make a firm intention to make an offer or announce that it will not proceed, unless the deadline is extended.

Stifel Sees $200M In Potential Synergies

According to TheFly, Stifel said the acquisition would give Altria direct access to international markets, strengthen its smoke-free product portfolio and provide additional benefits from customs duty refunds.

The firm said the deal was “no doubt accretive,” given Imperial’s lower valuation and estimated synergies of around $200 million. Stifel maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on Altria with an $82 price target. This represents a 10% upside from current levels.

Meanwhile, Jefferies said Altria could consider selling its 8.1% stake in AB InBev, valued at $12.8 billion, to fund Imperial’s acquisition.

Citi Sees Strategic Benefits

Citi said the potential acquisition has “considerable strategic logic,” as it would diversify Altria’s traditional cigarette business and significantly expand its presence in next-generation tobacco and nicotine products. The firm does not anticipate any difficulties for Altria in financing the acquisition.

Citi maintained its ‘Hold’ rating on MO with a $72 price target. MO has a 12-month consensus price target of $74.75, according to Koyfin. Four of the 11 analysts covering the stock have a ‘Buy’ rating, six have a ‘Hold’ rating, and two have a ‘Sell’ rating.

Retail’s Take On Potential Acquisition

Retail sentiment surrounding MO on Stocktwits turned ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘high’ message volumes.

MO shares have gained about 30% so far in 2026.

data.title: Gold pares gains as Fed-hike risks linger, eyes first weekly rise in three weeks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold pares gains after jumping over 3% earlier in the session
  • Spot silver up nearly 5%, off $38.18/oz lows hit on Wednesday
  • Gold, silver, platinum eye first weekly gain in three weeks

By Sherin Sans

Gold pared gains on Friday as a firm US dollar, rising Treasury yields and a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook kept investors cautious, but bullion remained on track for its first weekly gain in three as bargain buying lifted prices from a 15-month low hit earlier this week.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to $3,635.81 per ounce by 9:34 a.m. ET (1434 GMT), having risen more than 3% earlier in the session. The metal was on track for a weekly gain of nearly 3% after posting losses in the previous two weeks.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.9% to $3,634.30 per ounce.

"This recent bounce looks more like short-covering/profit taking than a change in trend. The Fed is still hiking, real yields are high and the dollar is near multi-month highs. Until one of those shifts, rallies toward $3,750–3,800 could attract sellers," said Zain Vawda, market analyst at Audacity Capital.

The dollar was still close to its highest level in 22 months, making dollar-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield rose and was off its recent lows.

Gold fell to its lowest level since late August 2025, at $3,426.35 per ounce, on Wednesday after strong US inflation data boosted expectations that the Fed will keep raising interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

"A return to $5,000 is possible, but not in the first half of the year. Gold needs the Fed to stop hiking and the dollar to roll over. If that happens by mid-2027, a recovery toward $4,500 is realistic," Vawda added.

Rising interest rates diminish gold's appeal by boosting returns on competing interest-bearing assets.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in key Asian hubs improved this week, with jewellery and investment buying picking up in India, while strong retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

Spot silver climbed 5.4% to $43.73 per ounce, platinum gained 2.5% to $1,323.33 per ounce and palladium rose 2.7% to $896.25 per ounce.

All three metals were poised for weekly gains.

data.title: Bayhorse Silver Underground Drilling Program Results Four IP Targets
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Bayhorse Silver Inc, (TSXV: BHS) (OTCQB: BHSIF) (FSE: 7KXN) (the "Company" or "Bayhorse") reports on the results received for six drill holes from its seven underground drill holes totaling 886m (2922 ft) into four IP targets that were identified during its 2025 Bayhorse IP survey (Figure 1). The results from one remaining drill hole is pending. Two holes, CR2-2026-1 and CR2-2026-2 were drilled south at shallow angles into IP target CR-2, that was located 121 - 150 m (400 - 495 ft) south of the underground drill station.

Figure 1 Underground drill holes

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Drill holes CR1-2026-1 and CR1-2026-2 and MW2-2026-00 were drilled into and beside IP anomaly CR-1 centered underneath the middle of and trending NW of the known Mine workings, and holes MW-1 and MW-2 were targeted into two IP targets below and 90 m (297 ft) to the east of the underground drill station at shallower angles than DDH BH24-01.

Minor silver and copper values were intersected in three holes as tabulated below.

There were no reportable results from drill holes CR2-2026-1 and CR2-2026-2, that mainly encountered brecciation along the majority of its length.

Each drill hole intersected the middle of the calculated down dip center elevation of the anomalies. Drill holes into the CR-1 anomaly intersected relatively competent ground, while drill holes into the CR-2 anomaly met with extremely difficult ground conditions.

Diamond drill hole MW-2-2026-00, was planned to intersect the northern, lower rhyolite body at 500 ft downhole and drilled at a 45 dg dip to 130 m (429 ft) north from the drill station and 70 m (231 ft) west of the ground water test well 2024 MW-2 to test the westward extension of a reported 1.5 m (5 ft) grading 1104 g/t (35.46 opt) silver and 1.5 m (5 ft) 770 g/t (23.12 opt) silver mineralization within a mineralized 9 m (30 ft ) zone estimated between 21 - 30 m (70 - 100 ft) downhole as reported in the Company's news release BHS2025-12. Due to ground conditions, this drill hole was terminated at a downhole depth of 365 ft.

The top of the silver bearing rhyolite has been cut and offset by east-directed thrusting, and the overlying segment dyke that has been historically mined has been displaced to the south a minimum of 60 m (200) with a vertical displacement identified by drilling of a minimum 20 m (66 ft). Subsequently, there is significant faulting and fault gouge between the northern and southerly displaced rhyolite section resulting from the displacement of the upper mineralized section to the south. Due to the significant vertical and horizontal structural offset of the rhyolite body, it was only possible to drill low angle holes (-30 to -45 degrees) to intercept the northern section of the mineralized rhyolite from the underground drill station. This prevented any drilling of the northern underlying segment of mineralization, which is estimated to be 60-70 m (198 - 230 ft) north of, and 20-30 m (66-100 ft) below, the bottom of the south displaced section at the 706 m (2330 ft) above sea level.

Figure 2. Underground drill traces over IP anomalies. Figure 1. Thrusting has offset both the rhyolite and its related silver mineralization a minimum 60 m (200 ft) to the south where the underground mining is planned to take place.

As a result, and to minimize encountering difficult ground conditions experienced from underground, the Company plans to complete drilling these targets from surface drill sites when the surface drill permit is received. The Company and its engineering consultant continue to engage with DOGAMI for the approval of its surface drill permit, however, there can be no assurance that the Company will receive those permits on a timely basis.

The ongoing drilling program directed towards expanding the Bayhorse mineralized zone has confirmed Dr Clay Conway's structural and geological mapping of the Bayhorse Silver Mine where the top of the silver bearing rhyolite dyke has been cut and offset by east-directed thrusting, and the overlying segment has been displaced to the south.

This displaced historically mined section, with an estimated vertical extent of 40 m (130 ft) and a minimum east-west extent of 227 m (750 ft) and average thickness of between 45 m and 60m (150 - 200 ft). As disclosed in the Company's news release BHS2026-19.

Bayhorse CEO Graeme O'Neill comments "During the DOGAMI permitting delay the Company engaged specialist engineering personal, along with Steinert technical personnel to complete the Ore-Sorter repairs that was received from the rental in an inoperative condition. Twenty-seven samples from the pre-sorting crushed bulk sample test have been submitted for rush assay. The balance of sorting is expected to be completed mid-December and the sorted select and reject samples will be submitted for assay to get an accurate grade for the 15 tons of the 25 ton bulk sample test."

About Bayhorse Silver Inc.

Bayhorse Silver Inc. is an exploration and production company with a 100% interest in the historic Bayhorse Silver Mine located in Oregon, USA with a National Instrument 43-101 inferred resource of 292,300 tons at a grade of 21.65 opt (673 g/t) for 6.3 million ounces of silver. (Turner et al. 2018) and the Pegasus Project, in Washington County, Idaho. The Bayhorse Silver Mine and the Pegasus Porphyry Copper Project are 44 km southwest of Hercules Metals' porphyry copper discovery. The Bayhorse Mine is a minimum environmental impact facility capable of processing at a mining rate of up to 200 tons/day that includes a state of the art 40 ton per hour Steinert Ore-Sorter that reduces waste rock entering the processing stream by up to 85%. The Company has established an up to 60 ton/day mill and standard flotation processing facility in nearby Payette County, Idaho, USA with an offtake agreement in place with Ocean Partners UK Limited. data.title: Wall Street climbs higher on Black Friday
data.description:
Wall Street climbed higher on Black Friday as major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week, with traders reassessing positions amid lighter trading volumes.

The blue-chip Dow was last +0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite was last +0.8%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, nine of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with energy leading the way higher, while health care has been the weakest area.

Moreover, the economic calendar remains light for the session as the U.S. stock markets will close early on Friday for the Black Friday holiday session.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield added 2 basis points to 4.66%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield shifted up 3 basis points to 4.89%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield moved higher by 4 basis points to 5.29%.

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Sandisk advanced +8.5%, while shares of Vertex Pharmaceuticals dropped -9.3%.

data.title: Vertex falls on “disappointing” FDA delay on kidney drug review; Vera rises
data.description:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals traded lower on Friday, and rival Vera Therapeutics gained after the U.S. FDA extended its review of the former’s kidney disease drug povetacicept, a decision Leerink Partners identified as “quite disappointing.”

Announcing the revised Feb. 28 target action date issued in connection with its Biologics License Application for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy, Vertex on Wednesday attributed the delay to an information request from the FDA.

The company's stock lost more than 10% after the announcement, its worst intra-day performance since August 2025.

Vera Therapeutics , whose once-weekly injectable branded as Trutakna received the U.S. accelerated approval for IgA nephropathy in July, added ~15% in reaction, recording its best intraday gain since June 2025.

Noting the review extension as “quite disappointing,” Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger, who has an Outperform rating on Vertex , remained hopeful. “We now assume that pove will be approved within the next three months,” Risinger wrote, according to Bloomberg.“Although we cannot predict the FDA label, we are hoping that if blood monitoring is required, it is infrequent and thus does not materially impact commercial prospects,” the analyst added.

Baird analyst Brian Skorney, who has an Underperform rating on Vertex , argued that the delay allows rivals Vera and Otsuka Holdings to extend their lead in the IgAN market with their directly competitive, approved drugs. “In a worst-case scenario, the FDA request is looking closer at potential need for IgG monitoring for povetacicept,” Skorney added.

Raymond James analyst Christopher Raymond argued that the insufficient details provided on the reason for the delay are "likely to fuel bearish speculation around the drug’s safety profile.” Raymond, who has a Market Perform rating on VRTX, says he “can’t argue that this program does not now carry a meaningfully higher level of risk.”

data.title: Bigger Generali stake among options for UniCredit as partnership expands, sources say
data.description:
UniCredit has been weighing a possible increase of its 9% stake in Generali , four people close to the matter said, as Italy's second-biggest bank and the country's largest insurer discuss new commercial accords.

The Generali investment has so far been the only move by UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel in Italy's fast-consolidating banking market.

The veteran dealmaker has just secured control of Germany's Commerzbank , and says UniCredit will grow its domestic market share without any major acquisitions.

Meanwhile, the Generali stake has positioned UniCredit as a counterweight to its main rival Intesa Sanpaolo - which looks set to become the biggest Generali shareholder through a takeover of Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) .

Two of the four people said UniCredit could raise its Generali holding towards the 13.4% stake which is expected to pass from MPS into Intesa's hands.

The outcome of UniCredit's deliberations remains uncertain.

UniCredit and Generali both declined to comment.

By exercising significant influence over Generali, without control, Intesa can book the insurer's profits in its earnings in proportion to the stake, under international accounting rules.

Independent of its Generali stake coming from the MPS deal, Intesa has also built a further 3% stake in the insurer, which it has said it will dispose of.

Intesa CEO Carlo Messina has said he would be happy for UniCredit and Generali to find ways to generate profits together.

UniCredit first unveiled a 4.1% Generali stake , before building it up to the current 9.05%. Crossing 10% requires supervisory approval.

UniCredit and Generali, which already partner in eastern Europe, have been discussing closer commercial ties.

On November 9, Orcel said it was up to Generali to decide whether to accept UniCredit's help, adding that he hoped an agreement could be reached in the coming months.

He has repeatedly said such partnerships do not require UniCredit to control Generali, or a formal combination.

Orcel last week put the value of closer cooperation between UniCredit and Generali at €1.5-€2.0 billion ($1.6-$2.2 billion), with Generali remaining independent and simply agreeing to "innovative" forms of partnership.

A day later, Generali CEO Philippe Donnet said the insurer agrees with Orcel's view of the value the two companies can generate together.($1 = 0.9136 euros)
